paragraphs.text: Dear sisters and elders, it's going to be a great day today. I've already heard from enough of you to know that our next series of audio messages are going to be on how we break free from bad habits and build good ones to create powerful and positive structure in our lives.
I'm excited to share my thoughts with you about this science behind habit creation and habit change. And it is science.
Over the last 10 years, there have been numerous university studies that have been published in highly prestigious journals and many, many books written by the researchers based on those studies.

I've been a very interested student of this research because so much of my life has been about how we can change to become more than we ever thought we could or even more than our environment would suggest was possible.

I'll be sharing thoughts from many of these great researchers, but three writers particularly have been very influential in helping me arrive at the understanding that I now have and will share with you over the next five or six days. I'll introduce those writers and researchers to you when the time comes.

I expect that I'll be continuing to do this audio messaging through the rest of my mission. So I'm going to go ahead and give this activity a name. This is now going to be called The Quezon City North Mission Podcast. And we'll try to do it five or six days every week and maybe more if the need arises.

I want you to know this is hard work. It's hard work to do a five or six day a week podcast, even if it's a short one. But as we also know, hard choices equals easy life and easy choices equals hard life. I will make the hard choices. How about you?

That's a question you're going to have to ask yourself several times every day the rest of your life. But if you make the right decision on that question, you're going to have a much easier and a lot better life.

Now for a brief update, I just learned from our dear Elder Tala that he and the other missionaries from Australia will finally be able to return to Australia. They'll fly out tonight and arrive tomorrow morning in Brisbane, Australia. And then they're going to be in quarantine for 14 days.
Then they'll be reassigned to missions in Australia if they have enough time left to serve on their missions or if they don't, they'll be returned home to get on with the rest of their life.

Interestingly, the plane that will take them to Australia will be coming from Africa with 36 Filipino missionaries who were serving in missions there in Africa. They'll be quarantined at the MTC for 14 days and then will return to their homes to wait for things to clear up a little bit here in the Philippines relative to the lockdowns.
And then when things have cleared up a little bit, they'll either be reassigned to missions here in the Philippines or they'll be released if their missions are close to coming to an end.
These are truly historic times and we don't know from one week to the next what's going to happen for sure. But we are sure what will happen in all things that really matter.

This reminds me of a favorite talk in General Conference by Elder Neil L. Anderson. It's titled, "You Know Enough." And Elder Anderson shared his talk in October of 2008. I want to share a brief part of his talk with you now, but recommend that you listen to all of it when you get some time this weekend.

Quote, "Nearly 40 years ago as I contemplated the challenge of a mission, I felt very inadequate and unprepared. I remember praying, 'Heavenly Father, how can I serve a mission when I know so little?' I believed in the church, but I felt my spiritual knowledge was very limited."
As I prayed, the feeling came, "you don't know everything, but you know enough." That reassurance gave me the courage to take the next step into the mission field.

Our spiritual journey is the process of a lifetime. We do not know everything in the beginning or even along the way. Our conversion comes step by step, line upon line. We first build a foundation of faith in the Lord Jesus Christ.

We treasure the principles and the ordinances of repentance, baptism, and receiving the gift of the Holy Ghost. We include a continuing commitment to prayer, a willingness to be obedient, and an ongoing witness of the Book of Mormon. The Book of Mormon is powerful spiritual nourishment.

We then remain steady and patient as we progress through mortality. At times the Lord's answer will be, "you don't know everything, but you know enough." Enough to keep the commandments and to do what is right.
Remember Nephi's words, "I know that he loveth his children. Nevertheless, I do not know the meaning of all things."
Close quote from Elder Anderson.

And so my dear elders and sisters, it's true that we don't know the meaning of all things or why some things happen that interrupt our righteous desires or our inspired plans. But we do know enough to know like Nephi that God loveth his children and he loveth you.

Elders and sisters, make it a great day today through your choice to be of service to others, to be kind and humble. Because you know enough to know that this will please your Father in heaven and it will make you happy. We love you.
